think_procedure: Identify what the knob controls: innodb_lru_scan_depth is an InnoDB parameter that controls how many pages the page cleaner scans in the buffer pool LRU list per iteration.
Check if the knob is numeric and ordered: It is an integer-valued knob with a natural ordering (larger values mean scanning more pages).

Determine if there are documented special sentinel values (e.g., -1, 0) that change the semantics qualitatively (like disabling a feature or switching to auto-tuning) instead of just being the lower/upper bound of the normal range.

Consult MySQL/InnoDB documentation and known defaults: innodb_lru_scan_depth has a positive integer range (e.g., minimum 1) and no documented meaning for 0 or negative values; it does not have a value that disables LRU scanning or changes it to a fundamentally different mode.

Conclude whether any value breaks the natural numeric order by acting as a special mode: Since no such sentinel value exists and all valid values behave as regular numeric tuning of the same mechanism, it is not a special knob under the given definition.
